BREAKING: Japan's exports jumped +20.5% YoY in October, to a record $74 billion, the 2nd-largest monthly increase since October 2022.

Japan’s exports have now grown for 14 consecutive months, the longest streak since 2021-2023.

The surge was led by semiconductor manufacturing equipment shipments, which soared +49.7% YoY.

This was followed by electrical machinery exports, at +33.6% YoY growth, reflecting strong global investment in AI infrastructure.

Among regions, exports to Taiwan led with +42.7% YoY growth, followed by ASEAN at +34.7%, the US at +23.9%, the EU at +22.1%, and China at +13.3%.

Global chip demand is transforming the Japanese economy.

BREAKING: Global fund managers cut their technology exposure by -25 percentage points in early November, to a net 12%, their biggest monthly decline since June 2006.

This marks even a larger monthly decline than during the 2022 bear market or the 2008 Financial Crisis.

As a result, technology is no longer the most overweight sector among fund managers.

The largest overweight positions are currently in Pharmaceuticals, at 34%, and Industrials, at 19%.

A record 38% of surveyed institutional investors believe companies are overinvesting, up from ~20% in January.

At the same time, 52% expect Big Tech companies to announce CapEx reductions over the next 6 months, up from 30% in October.

Institutional investors are rotating out of technology stocks at a rapid pace.

After past unfavorable signals, the S&P 500 was higher one year later only 23% of the time, with a median return of -15.6%.

Every sector also had a negative median return one year later, with some suffering much larger losses.
